chapter: Ellington colleagues, singers and world tours
title: Blanton's influence and later Ellington bassists
summary: Blanton, once a violinist, made the bass a solo instrument; Pettiford and Wendell Marshall followed.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Jimmy Blanton, I believe, is generally considered to have caused a Renaissance in bass playing a new approach and won new respect for the bass as an instrument in the orchestra, is that right?

Well originally Jimmy Blanton was a violin player. And when you think of his playing, you would think more or less of a violin player doing what we call pluck -- plucking his instrument. And that's the way that he played only on the bass he plucked his bass and then he would turn around and bow -- bow it also just like he had plucked the same notes that he had plucked, he was very ingenious in that way.
Did he have any specific influence over -- or inspiration for his approach to the bass, do you know?

I don't think so, he was just a natural. He just -- he could play for hours so if you had influences or patterns that you were following, you'd run out of them if it wasn't your own, but he could play for hours, in fact he did quite a bit of that, he'd go in these after hour places,
take his bass and just play and play and play.
But a bass player in Duke's band had a different kind of position, after Blanton, did he not. They were featured more often, weren't they?

Yes, well the next one, I think, was Pettiford, patterned after Blanton in soloing, see a bass didn't solo too much before Blanton. Not in the same way that Blanton soloed, the bass was usually just a bass and not a solo or a melody playing instrument. But Blanton could play melodies any kind of music on his bass, so he was very outstanding.
How did Pettiford come into the band?

Ah, I'm -- I think Pettiford, who came after Jimmy. See Jimmy got sick and he never returned, so they had to look for other bass players and they fooled around and took this one and that one until finally they landed on Pettiford, who was very good. And Pettiford went a step further, he did with a cello what Jimmy Blanton had done with a bass, made a sort of a solo thump instrument or plucking instrument out of the cello.
And did Wendell Marshall follow Oscar Pettiford into the band or was there someone inbetween?
Oh yes, there was Junior Raglin (Inaudible) Ragland-and --
Oh, yes there was a lot of them, yes.
I remember Wendell, Wendell was featured a lot, so --
Yeah, he was a nice bass player, too. But you see when somebody like Pettiford -- I mean somebody like Blanton -- it's hard to follow him. You can't follow him very easily.
Now Wendell Marshall is Blanton's cousin, that's it. And he did -- he had one of Blanton's bass. Yes, that's right.
